gates.evidence: The surface is s11 (Account Menu Sidebar), a standard utility menu, and the reward involves news reading across general categories (Top Stories, Entertainment, etc.) as seen in the core loop.
The reward is '15 minutes of ad-free reading' (resource: Ad-free Sprint), which is an in-app entitlement. No cash, gift cards, or external incentives are mentioned.
The proposal introduces a new 'Ad-free Sprint' option as an additive benefit. It does not use fake timers, 'support us' copy, or hostage framing of existing content.
The storyboard phase 'offer' specifies that the 'Simula MiniGameInvitation appears' and the user must tap the CTA 'Start Sprint' to participate.
The offer body states: 'Play a 15-second game to clear all ads from your news feed for a short sprint.' (Title: 'Go Ad-Free for 15 Minutes'). Both action and reward are clear.
The offer includes a 'No thanks' decline button, and the proposal notes that declining returns the user to the sidebar with no penalty.
The trigger is in the Account Menu Sidebar (s11), which is a navigation/settings boundary and does not interrupt an active reading experience or video stream.
Eligibility is restricted to 'Non-paying users currently exposed to standard ad density.'

scores.evidence: The reward (ad-free reading) directly addresses the high density of ads in the app, but placing it in the Account Menu (s11) is a proactive 'hub' placement rather than a reactive 'moment of need' (e.g., after closing an article ad).
The sprint preserves the news-reading flow and input (article detail views), takes nothing away from free users, and adds a helpful timer badge (ne2) to confirm the state.
The reward is strictly time-boxed to 15 minutes and limited to 3 sessions per day. This acts as a 'taste of premium' sampling effect for non-payers only.
Code-computed cost is $0.00 (no inference/COGS). One US view earns $0.009–$0.015. Ad-free reading is a zero-marginal-cost reward that is margin-safe.
The Account Menu Sidebar (s11) has an 'occasional' reach (m10). Most users spend their time in the Home News Feed (s02, s13), meaning a significant portion of DAU may never see this offer.
Maps to SIM-RWD using a button entry. While ad-suppression logic requires development, it fits the Simula SDK pattern of temporary entitlements.
Uses app-specific locations (s11 Sidebar, s02 Home) and references the AOL 'Game Partner'. The 'Ad-Free Sprint' concept is a standard TAX-2 implementation.
Proposal includes explicit caps (3/day) and a 60-minute cooldown (cooldownMin).
Identifies a primary metric (sprint sessions) and includes a 10% user-level holdout over 21 days with specific guardrail KPIs.

requiredChanges: Fix grounding of economy IDs (e42, e17) as they were flagged by the system as non-existent or misaligned with screen element IDs.
Introduce a secondary trigger or entry point on high-reach surfaces such as the Home News Feed (s02) or between article transitions to improve reach beyond 'occasional' sidebar users.
Define a clear success threshold for the primary KPI (Ad-free Sprint sessions started) relative to the holdout group.
parsed.topConcern: The placement in the Account Menu Sidebar (s11) has very low reach ('occasional' per the digest), which severely limits the revenue and engagement potential compared to a trigger within the core news feeds.
